bias_atlas.snapshot_source: computed in d4_bias_atlas from cache/arxiv_audit.jsonl (outputs/snapshot/ absent)

H4a.statement: Neutral filter for the mainstream fashion: NAME G_total in [0.95, 1.10] every year 2018-26; pooled 2024-26 TOST within [0.90, 1.11]; 2024 slope-change OR equal across ACC, REJ, WD.
H4a.falsification: pooled NAME G_total 90% CI outside [0.90, 1.11], or pool-specific break ORs differ at p < .05
H4a.notes: All nine yearly NAME total gains lie in [0.95, 1.10]; the pooled 90% CI [1.001, 1.041] is inside the equivalence margins; the Wald test does not reject equal pool breaks (p = 0.51) and the largest point difference is 0.061 on the log-OR scale, but no pairwise difference is TOST-equivalent at +/-0.1 (pairwise 90% CIs extend from -0.17 to +0.12): equality is not rejected rather than demonstrated. The pre-decision stages deplete NAME slightly (desk x exit 0.972) and the decision stage enriches it (1.050), but the decision gain is not identified against camera-ready edits (T4.2).

H4b.statement: Depletion of LLM and outsider markers: pooled 2024-26 G_total < 1 for the L-union and O-union; G_desk x G_exit < 1 for the L-union.
H4b.notes: L-union total 0.975 (95% CI 0.951-1.001; one-sided bootstrap p = 0.030) and pre-decision 0.982 (0.972-0.992); O-union total 0.807 (0.749-0.870). Depletion of L is small in absolute terms and is carried by title R24 words (0.807) and abstract style density (0.965); abstract markers as a union are near-neutral (0.993). Relative to the pre-LLM years, when the same markers were enriched among accepted papers (L-union total 1.154), the post-2024 total gain is 15% lower (ratio 0.845, 0.783-0.915). O depletion sits at the decision stage (0.812), which camera-ready edits can produce and the audit cannot bound (ALL-CAPS and sentence case unauditable); only ALL-CAPS is also depleted at exit (0.839).

H4c.statement: Accepted-only Kobak-style lower bound on LLM-styled abstracts understates the all-submission bound by >= 15% relative in each of 2024-26.
H4c.falsification: accepted-only bound >= 0.9 x all-submission bound in 2024 and 2025
H4c.notes: Pre-registered baseline: ratios 0.80 / 0.71 / 0.50 (2024/25/26), all <= 0.85, not falsified; accepted bound 12.8 / 8.7 / 3.0 pp vs all 16.0 / 12.2 / 6.0 pp. But the gap comes mostly from the accepted pool's higher and rising 2021-23 baseline (2.95 -> 3.54 -> 4.30% vs 3.35 -> 2.49 -> 3.12%), not from lower 2024-26 prevalence (2024: 17.8% vs 19.1%). With a post hoc baseline that excludes 2023 (whose camera-ready abstracts post-date ChatGPT), the F24 ratios are 0.90 / 0.90 / 0.99, i.e. on the falsification boundary; the >= 2-word variant (F24_2) stays below 0.86 in 2024-25. The plan's direction argument (camera-ready polishing can only raise accepted rates) does not cover the baseline years, where it works against it.

H4d.statement: Within NA (withdrawn vs rejected), NAME coefficient > 0 in the cross-section, <= 0 within last-position key, and the two differ.
H4d.notes: Cross-section +4.06 pp (se 0.96) vs within last-position key -0.70 pp (se 1.08); difference 4.77 pp (se 0.75; key-cluster bootstrap 3.21-6.24). The within estimate is <= 0 at the point but its CI reaches +1.4 pp. All robustness variants keep within < cross; adding topic100 FE shrinks the cross-section to +0.84 pp (so part of the excess is topic composition) and the difference to 2.59 pp (se 0.71). In 2018-23 the within estimate is +4.2 pp (se 2.8), so the pattern is a 2024-26 result.

H4e.statement: Accepted-only estimates fall within +/-10% of all-submission estimates for M metrics; deviations concentrate in O and L; each gap split into selection (desk, exit exact) and editing (audit).

atlas.statistic: Peak years of top-30 title fashions (agreement with all)

H4e.notes: 11/11 ratio-type M statistics lie within +/-10% (median |log ratio| 0.018); O 1/4 (median 0.160); L 7/9 (median 0.037; outliers R24 prevalence 0.81 and the Kobak bound 0.72). All M point estimates are inside +/-10%; two M 90% CIs cross the margin (snowclone share 0.91, 90% CI 0.77-1.04; ITS slope-change OR ratio 0.95, 0.90-1.01). Editing is separable only for auditable title features and is not bounded by the 331-pair audit (e.g. NAME editing log-ratio +0.042, interval -0.047 to +0.148).

decision_stage_bound.source: computed by d4_bias_atlas from cache/arxiv_audit.jsonl; outputs/snapshot/ (WP4) was not available
decision_stage_bound.gate: No title-feature acceptance gain is identified: every tipping point lies inside the audit DiD 95% CI.

desk_rejection_timing_2026.reason: 100.0% of 2026 desk rejections carry a modification timestamp on/after the decision date (median 2026-02-12 14:51:43.630000); the timestamp records a bulk post-decision update, not the desk-rejection date

deviations: Pooled gains are year-standardised (each year's stage prevalence weighted by its s0 size); raw pooling is reported as robustness. PLAN does not specify the pooling.
OTHER rows (71 in 2018 with unknown decision) are dropped from the D4 stage frame.
ALL-CAPS title = casing class all_caps (whole title in capitals); the scout stage pilot used the NAME lead orthography; that variant is reported as allcaps_name.

L-union = any binary L marker (title typography, R24, R26, F24, F26, abstract em dash); the continuous style density is reported separately and is not in the union. Em dash = abstract em dash (title em dash reported as secondary).
Year-specific style density re-implements the scout rule on the frozen scout style pool (analyses/d4_lexicon.json); selected words 123/150/223 for 2024/25/26.

Decision-stage tipping point accounts for accepted papers inside s2: D* = (P3 - P2)/(1 - a2). The plan's 1.8 pp pilot ignored the (1 - a2) factor; with it NAME's tipping point is 2.9 pp (total-gain tipping point 1.0 pp).

Snapshot module computed inside d4_bias_atlas from cache/arxiv_audit.jsonl (WP4 outputs absent). Only titles are auditable (no v1 abstracts cached); auditable = feature present in >= 10 accepted v1 and stored titles (pre-stated).
Colon premium: no accepted-only version exists; the published-only analogue is decided-only (ACC vs REJ).

Opener-entropy and JSD intervals use a random-selection band (pivot) instead of the paper bootstrap, which produced intervals excluding the point estimate (duplicates bias the unrarefied accepted set).
H4c: post hoc baseline sensitivity max(2021, 2022) added because ICLR 2023 camera-ready abstracts post-date ChatGPT.
H4d: primary population REJ u WD (2024-26), outcome = withdrawn incl. 2026 post-decision withdrawals; last position = max list position (D2 convention); controls year FE, log authors, llm_topic.
Early vs late 2026 desk rejections not testable: all 737 desk-rejection timestamps fall on/after the decision date (bulk update).
Desk-stage continuation-ratio logits fitted for 2024-26 only (2018-23 has 0-19 desk rejections a year).
language: Associational; declared profile keys are not persons; list positions are partition labels.
